Title:
LoopBridge: Should Prefill and Decode Loop Equally?

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
31 pages, 16 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers for the same number of loops during prefill and decode. Yet generation is strongly asymmetric: on chain-of-thought tasks at batch 1, prefill reads the prompt once in parallel and takes under 3% of wall time, while decoding runs token by token and takes over 97%. We ask whether prefill and decode should loop equally, and find that they should not: untying the two loop counts lets a model read the prompt with more loops and decode each answer token with fewer. Because naive untying fails on pretrained models, we introduce LoopBridge, a small adapter (2.4% of parameters) with RoPE-commuting key maps and linear value maps that serves any trained prefill/decode pair and folds into the prompt cache once. On Ouro-2.6B with one decode loop, four prefill loops raise the 11-benchmark average from 44.2 to 58.2, well above tied-loop distillation on the same data (49.5). On Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, LoopBridge with four prefill and two decode loops stays within 0.8 points of the four-loop model across eight benchmarks and matches its GSM8K accuracy at 2.0x end-to-end throughput. On Ouro-2.6B, most of the gain arrives within two to five prefill loops, and untying transfers to Ouro-1.4B, Thinking models, looped decision models, and 26.4B sparse-MoE models in vLLM (3/1 beats tied 1/1 distillation by 7.8 points on five 256K-1M and reasoning benchmarks; 3/2 retains 96.2% of 3/3 at 1.37x decode speed with zero overhead). Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/loopbridge
